c11_eng_h_cbse_05_004: Rajendra explains the science, but Gaitonde lives the story — and he shifted to a parallel present. Check: who experienced it?
c11_eng_h_cbse_05_005: Not every named person matters equally — Rajendra drives the plot; the ticket-checker just colours it. Check: who moves the story?
c11_eng_h_cbse_05_006: 'Alternate history' is the premise — the theme is reality branching like a quantum event. Check: premise or insight?
c11_eng_h_cbse_05_007: The train journey is an event — 'chance shapes history' is a theme. Check: what does it signify?
c11_eng_h_cbse_05_008: Imagery isn't only sight — 'stirred him to the depths' is inner sensation. Check: which sense is working?
c11_eng_h_cbse_05_009: The train isn't a comparison — it recurs at every reality-shift, so it's a symbol. Check: comparison or recurring sign?
c11_eng_h_cbse_05_010: 'De facto' isn't just 'of fact' — it means 'in practice, not officially'. Check: did you read the whole phrase?
c11_eng_h_cbse_05_011: Third conditional gets one 'would have' — 'if I had known, I would have told you'. Check: which clause takes 'had'?
c11_eng_h_cbse_05_012: Link the missed bullet to catastrophe theory — inference joins the history to the science. Check: did you connect both?
c11_eng_h_cbse_05_013: He didn't visit the past — he woke in a present that branched at Panipat. Check: travel or shift?
c11_eng_h_cbse_05_014: Use the story as evidence — analysing his method beats retelling his trip. Check: retell or apply?
c11_eng_h_cbse_05_015: Discussion explores perspectives with evidence — it's not a debate to win. Check: what methods overlap?
c11_eng_h_cbse_06_001: A fact is context only when you connect it — ask what it illuminates in the text. Check: so what?
c11_eng_h_cbse_06_002: In a play, talk is action — each line is a move in a power struggle. Check: what does the line do?
c11_eng_h_cbse_06_003: The cracked mug isn't just a prop — the school's little objects press on dignity. Check: what feeling does it build?
c11_eng_h_cbse_06_004: 'The Crock' is armour — the same man weeps over the Agamemnon. Check: persona or person?
c11_eng_h_cbse_06_005: The 'minor' characters carry this play — each one reveals a different Andrew. Check: what does each expose?
c11_eng_h_cbse_06_006: The gift isn't the theme — the human connection it carries is. Check: what does it mean?
c11_eng_h_cbse_06_007: 'Tibetan mastiffs' is a detail — the theme is instinct meeting intrusion. Check: element or concern?
c11_eng_h_cbse_06_008: Listen for the tap of the ruler — imagery isn't only what you see. Check: which sense is struck?
c11_eng_h_cbse_06_009: Surprise isn't irony — the system rewarding Frank over excellence is. Check: what contradicts what?
c11_eng_h_cbse_06_010: Don't memorise definitions — deduce 'agog' from Taplow's anxious wait. Check: what do the clues say?
c11_eng_h_cbse_06_011: Labelling 'past tense' isn't enough — say what the verb's force does here. Check: what's the effect?
c11_eng_h_cbse_06_012: Inference isn't opinion — anchor it to a line like 'my head began to throb'. Check: which line supports it?
c11_eng_h_cbse_06_013: The pedant persona is armour — the aspirin moment lets the private man through. Check: mask or man?
c11_eng_h_cbse_06_014: A character sketch uses this text — not a teacher you once had. Check: whose evidence?
c11_eng_h_cbse_06_015: Good discussion builds on others and can change your mind — thinking together, not winning. Check: did you revise a view?
c11_eng_h_cbse_07_001: The truck didn't send him to 1761 — it shifted his consciousness to a branched present. Check: which physics?
c11_eng_h_cbse_07_002: Listing events is plot — structure is the order the telling chooses. Check: told or telling?
c11_eng_h_cbse_07_003: The alternate Bombay is a constructed setting — 'familiar' vs 'alien' words build the mood. Check: which details construct it?
c11_eng_h_cbse_07_004: The history is the lens, not the man — analyse how his training drives the verifying. Check: whose method?
c11_eng_h_cbse_07_005: Don't invent a biography — ask what the character does for the story. Check: function or life story?
c11_eng_h_cbse_07_006: It isn't a what-if fantasy — both histories are real on different branches. Check: fantasy or physics?
c11_eng_h_cbse_07_007: 'Eyewitness accounts' is a topic — 'the unreliability of eyewitness accounts' is a theme. Check: can it be a claim?
c11_eng_h_cbse_07_008: The smells of alternate Bombay aren't decoration — they prove the world is real. Check: what work does it do?
c11_eng_h_cbse_07_009: The train recurs at every reality-shift — that's symbol, not metaphor. Check: one-off or structural?
c11_eng_h_cbse_07_010: Watch the small words — 'real' changes meaning as the story unfolds. Check: verified how?
c11_eng_h_cbse_07_011: Tense is a choice here — past perfect marks 1761, conditionals mark the counterfactual. Check: which layer?
c11_eng_h_cbse_07_012: Even the literal answer needs a citation — inference is disciplined, not free. Check: what's your line?
c11_eng_h_cbse_07_013: The physics isn't decorative — the many-worlds must be literally true inside the story. Check: mechanism or ornament?
